subject: Greystone: follow-up on pen-test remediation evidence
messages:
From: Alex Hammond <alex.hammond@greystone.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@greystone.com
Date: 2026-11-02T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Pen-test follow-up: request for remediation evidence and artifacts

Vanessa —

Thanks again for the demo last week and for walking through the penetration test summary. Our security team finished their review of the remediation notes and has two asks before we close the ticket:

1) Can you provide screenshots or short screencasts showing the fix for the token cache eviction issue (steps + before/after)?
2) We need a snippet of the runtime config you applied (the exact flag toggles and values) plus the internal ticket reference that tracked the fix (so we can tie it to our audit).

We aim to get this into our evidence bundle for SOC 2 readiness by Friday. If there are compensating controls (WAF rule or temporary rate-limiting) that were applied while remediation shipped, please call those out.

Appreciate a compressed artifact or a Drive folder link.

—Alex
Alex Hammond
Director, Information Security
Greystone Financial
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Hammond <alex.hammond@greystone.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-03T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pen-test follow-up: request for remediation evidence and artifacts

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Putting the right folks on this thread: Aditya (solutions lead) will collate screenshots and the walkthrough; Karthik (security engineering) will attach the runtime config and the remediation ticket; Monica (customer success) will link the Drive folder and confirm delivery SLA.

Plan: we will assemble a single evidence bundle (zip) that includes: short mp4 screencasts (screen capture, redacting any customer data), annotated screenshots (before/after), the exact runtime_config.yaml snippet we applied, and the internal JIRA ticket that tracked the fix. Karthik also noted we applied a temporary rate-limit at the edge and an additional WAF rule while the fix shipped — we'll document the TTL and rule id.

Target delivery: EOD Thursday (2026-11-05) PST. If Greystone needs anything earlier for the SOC 2 pack, flag here and we can prioritize.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
From: Alex Hammond <alex.hammond@greystone.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@greystone.com
Date: 2026-11-04T08:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pen-test follow-up: request for remediation evidence and artifacts

Vanessa —

That plan works. A couple of clarifications from our security reviewer:
- For the runtime config snippet, they want the exact changelist (diff) that was applied to production — if you can include the git commit hash or a link to the change, that helps.
- For the rate-limiting compensating control, they prefer a short note on monitoring (what metric/alert was used to detect regression) and if any automated rollback was configured.

Also, please make sure any MP4s/screenshots have timestamps visible or in the filename so our auditors can correlate artifacts to the remediation window.

Appreciate the tight turnaround.

—Alex
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Hammond <alex.hammond@greystone.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-05T16:38:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Pen-test follow-up: request for remediation evidence and artifacts

Alex / Greystone security team —

Attached is a consolidated evidence bundle and summary. Quick notes first:

- Attachments included (in Drive folder and zipped): greystone_pt_fixes_screenshots.zip (annotated before/after PNGs, MP4 walkthroughs), runtime_config_snippet.yaml (exact file applied), and a pointer to our internal remediation ticket (JIRA-4523).
- Git commit: 7f4c2d9 (PR #1987) — this PR contains the cache eviction fix; link: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/runtime/commit/7f4c2d9
- Compensating controls applied during remediation window:
  * Edge rate-limiting policy (RL-omega-23) — threshold 120 req/min per IP; monitored by Prometheus alert rule redwood.rate_limit.violation (>5/min sustained).
  * WAF rule added (WAF-2026-17) to block malformed auth headers observed in the pentest.
- Monitoring / rollback: we had an automated canary rollback configured in our deploy pipeline (rollback if 5xx rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes). During remediation we had a dashboard panel (DashID: dash-prod-ops-09) and a PagerDuty escalation set for the release window.
- Evidence details: all screenshots/MP4 filenames include timestamps in UTC; the runtime_config_snippet.yaml contains the exact flags we flipped (cache.eviction_policy: strict, cache.max_entries: 512).

Drive link (read-only): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2bGreystoneEvidence
JIRA ticket (internal): https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RW-4523

If you need a signed attestation or a short cover note for your SOC 2 binder, we can produce that (security leadership signature). Let us know whether you want the attestation and if it should reference the JIRA ticket and commit.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Security Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
